newsitem.title: USA: Boeing to offer new version of 767 airplane.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to offer new version of 767 airplane.

text.p: Boeing Co said it plans to offer its customers a new version of its 767 commercial airplane, dubbed the 767-400ERX.
The 767-400ERX's size would be between the 767-300 and the 777-200. New features would include a longer fuselage, added wing span, increased takeoff weight capability and new main landing gear.
The 767-400ERX would boost the number of seats from the current 767-300 by 10- to 15-percent, holding 245 passengers versus 218 in the -300 version.
Its range, about 6,500 statute miles, would allow it to fly the majority of routes now being served by the 767-300ER.
"This commonality will ensure a virtually transparent addition to existing 767 fleets and minimal impact to existing 757 fleets," said Ed Renouard, general manager of 747/767 programs.
If a sufficient number of orders are received, the company would begin production with a tentative target delivery date in the year 2000, Boeing said in a statement.
